fact: Jonathan Taylor's 2021 season is the counterintuitive one here: his 106.5 rushing yards per game is actually the lowest of these four seasons, yet his 18 rushing touchdowns is the highest — the 17-game season gave him an extra game, and a huge share of his team's goal-line work. Adrian Peterson's 2012 MVP season (131.1 YPG) is the opposite profile: gaining more yards per game than anyone here, but with the fewest touchdowns.
source: Pro Football Reference / StatMuse season totals. Yards-per-game computed from confirmed season yardage ÷ games played.
quarantineReason: Target sits mid-axis on both stats; a centre click scores 75 and beats an informed guess (lift -5). Taylor 2021 is not an outlier vs its anchors — the rushing-title season needs anchors that are not also elite rushers.

fact: Scottie Pippen's 2.0 steals and 0.8 blocks a game is a genuinely rare wing profile — enough blocks to suggest a rim-protecting big, delivered by a 6'8" forward who also picked pockets like a guard. Dikembe Mutombo (0.4 / 2.8) and John Stockton (2.2 / 0.2) are the two specialist extremes this pairing usually produces: a pure rim-protector and a pure ball-hawk. Hakeem Olajuwon (1.7 / 3.1) is the rare exception who tops both — a center with a guard's hands and a shot-blocker's timing.
quarantineReason: Steals and blocks both compress into a ~3-unit axis, so every guess is close in normalised terms. Lift 29. Needs a stat pair with more dynamic range.

xLabel: Career field goal attempts per game
fact: Michael Jordan took more shots per game (22.9) than anyone else here — even more than Allen Iverson (21.8), the standard reference for a pure volume scorer. But his efficiency (56.9 TS%) sits well below the elite tier: Stephen Curry (62.6) gets nearly as many shots up at a far higher efficiency, and DeAndre Jordan (64.4) shows the opposite extreme — a role player who barely shoots (5.1 attempts a game) but converts at an absurd rate, mostly dunks and putbacks. Jordan's greatness came from volume and shot difficulty, not from posting efficiency numbers like the specialists at either end of this chart.
source: StatMuse career true shooting percentage and field goal attempts per game (regular season).
quarantineReason: TS% has a narrow real spread (48-68) and Jordan sits mid-pack in it, so the y-axis carries almost no signal. Lift 22.

fact: Pedro Martinez struck out 10.04 batters per nine innings — essentially Randy Johnson territory (10.61) and more than Nolan Ryan's 9.55 — while walking only 2.42, closer to Greg Maddux, the control archetype at 1.80, than to either power pitcher. That combination is the entire argument for Pedro. Ryan bought his strikeouts with 4.67 walks per nine, nearly double Pedro's rate; Maddux bought his control by striking out 6.06, barely half as many. Pedro refused the trade. In 1999 he struck out 313 batters and walked 37.
source: StatMuse career K/9 and BB/9; 1999 season strikeout and walk totals.
quarantineReason: Both rate stats span <8 units; Pedro is extreme on K/9 but the anchors are too close to him. Lift 23.

fact: Randy Moss is the definitive deep threat of his era and he averaged 15.6 yards a catch — two full yards below DeSean Jackson's 17.6, and less than a yard above Jerry Rice's 14.8. The reputation didn't come from where the catches started, it came from where they ended: 156 receiving touchdowns, second-most all time. Wes Welker is the archetype's opposite pole — 903 catches, nearly Moss's total, at 11.0 yards each. "Deep threat" describes what a defense is afraid of, not what the average play actually gains.
source: StatMuse career receptions, yards per reception, and receiving touchdowns.
quarantineReason: Y/R spans 8-20 for essentially every receiver and Moss is mid-range in it; receptions alone carry the question. Centre click scores 65, lift 1.
